Read the inferential uncertainty that Salmon writes

Source: R/uncertainty-io.R
inferential-io.Rd

Salmon quantifies how well each transcript abundance is determined by the reads, and writes that information next to quant.sf:

  • read_inferential_replicates() reads the Gibbs (--numGibbsSamples) or bootstrap (--numBootstraps) replicates from aux_info/bootstrap/ (the format is identical in Salmon 1.x and in the Rust rewrite, Salmon 2). It returns a list with one transcript x sample matrix of counts per replicate, the layout used by productive_fraction() and add_uncertainty(). The samples are read one at a time, so memory holds the result and the replicates of a single sample. When the samples have different numbers of replicates, the smallest number is kept. The mean and variance over the kept replicates of every transcript, including those left out by transcripts, are recorded in the moments attribute: inferential_overdispersion() estimates its prior from them, so it does not depend on which transcripts are kept.

  • equivalence_support() reads the equivalence classes (--dumpEq, aux_info/eq_classes.txt.gz) and reports, for every transcript, how many of its fragments are compatible with no other transcript.

  • salmon_run_qc() reads aux_info/meta_info.json and reports the mapping rate, the library type, whether the optimiser converged and how many replicates were drawn.

  • inferential_replicates_table() and as_inferential_replicates() convert the list of replicates to and from a long table (one row per transcript, sample and replicate), which can be stored as Parquet with write_parquet() and read back with read_parquet(), for example to exchange them with other tools. inferential_moments_table() converts the moments attribute to a table in the same way (one row per transcript and sample); pass it to the moments argument of as_inferential_replicates() to restore it. The long table takes several times the memory of the replicates: to save the replicates of an object, use write_isoformic(), which writes one wide file per draw. Both apply the selection of the replicates of a subset x[i, j] (see IsoformicExperiment): the replicate table holds the kept transcripts and samples only, the moment table the kept samples (the moments keep every transcript). The selection is an attribute of the unmodified x@metadata$inf_reps: a list operation such as lapply() or [ drops it, and the list then holds the draws of the parent. Pass the object as x (alone, or with such a list as reps) to read the draws of its transcripts and samples in every case.

The functions also read Oarfish output (see read_oarfish()): its bootstrap replicates (.infreps.pq), its unique and ambiguous read counts (.ambig_info.tsv, n_classes is then NA) and its run metadata (.meta_info.json). One call reads the output of one tool.

Usage

read_inferential_replicates(
  paths,
  transcripts = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  ignore_after_bar = TRUE
)

equivalence_support(paths, transcripts = NULL, ignore_after_bar = TRUE)

salmon_run_qc(paths, min_percent_mapped = 50)

inferential_replicates_table(reps = NULL, x = NULL)

inferential_moments_table(reps = NULL, x = NULL)

as_inferential_replicates(table, samp_type = "gibbs", moments = NULL)

Arguments

paths

Character vector of Salmon output directories (containing quant.sf) or paths to quant.sf files, or Oarfish output prefixes. Names, when present, are the sample IDs; otherwise the directory name (or the prefix) is used.

transcripts

Optional transcript IDs to keep. Reading every transcript of a human annotation for many samples takes gigabytes of memory, so add_uncertainty() only reads the expressed ones.

n_draws

Number of replicates to keep (the first ones). NULL keeps all of them; a number above the replicates available keeps all of them, with a message.

ignore_after_bar

Logical. Keep only the part of transcript names before the first | (GENCODE FASTA headers used as Salmon references).

min_percent_mapped

Samples below this mapping rate (percent) get the low_mapping_rate flag in salmon_run_qc().

reps

A list of transcript x sample count matrices, one per replicate. In inferential_replicates_table() and inferential_moments_table(), it defaults to x@metadata$inf_reps when x is given.

x

Optional IsoformicExperiment. When given, the replicates are read as those of its transcripts and samples, matched by ID, even when reps lost the selection of a subset.

table

A long table with transcript_id, sample_id, draw and count columns, as returned by inferential_replicates_table().

samp_type

Replicate type recorded on the result, "gibbs" or "bootstrap".

moments

Optional table of inferential_moments_table() (columns transcript_id, sample_id, n_draws, mean and var) to record as the moments attribute of the result.

Value

  • read_inferential_replicates(): a list of numeric matrices (transcripts by samples, counts) with the replicate type ("gibbs" or "bootstrap") in the samp_type attribute and the moments of every transcript in the moments attribute (a list with the mean and var matrices, transcripts by samples, and the number of replicates n).

  • inferential_replicates_table(): a tibble with transcript_id, sample_id, draw and count. as_inferential_replicates() is its inverse. inferential_moments_table(): a tibble with transcript_id, sample_id, n_draws, mean and var.

  • equivalence_support(): a tibble with one row per transcript: transcript_id, n_classes (mean number of equivalence classes that contain the transcript, per sample), n_fragments and n_unique_fragments (summed over samples), unique_fraction (share of the fragments of the transcript that map to it alone) and n_samples (samples with equivalence classes).

  • salmon_run_qc(): a tibble with one row per sample: sample_id, salmon_version, library_type, detected_library_type, num_processed, num_mapped, percent_mapped, replicate_type, num_replicates, optimiser, em_converged, seq_bias_correct, gc_bias_correct, pos_bias_correct, frag_length_mean, frag_length_sd and qc_flag (low_mapping_rate, no_replicates and em_not_converged, separated by ;, or NA). For Oarfish output the columns are sample_id, num_processed, num_mapped, percent_mapped, replicate_type, num_replicates, optimiser, alignment_source, prob_model and qc_flag, and the tool attribute is "oarfish".

Examples

quant_dirs <- list.files(
  system.file("extdata", "mini_quants", package = "isoformic"),
  full.names = TRUE
)
names(quant_dirs) <- sub("_quant$", "", basename(quant_dirs))
# The bundled quantifications were made without replicates
salmon_run_qc(quant_dirs)[, c("sample_id", "percent_mapped", "qc_flag")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   sample_id   percent_mapped qc_flag         
#>   <chr>                <dbl> <chr>           
#> 1 SRR11498039          0.324 low_mapping_rate
#> 2 SRR11498040          0.422 low_mapping_rate
#> 3 SRR11498041          0.486 low_mapping_rate
#> 4 SRR11498077          0.449 low_mapping_rate
#> 5 SRR11498078          0.551 low_mapping_rate
#> 6 SRR11498079          0.507 low_mapping_rate
